items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Another fellow who became quite friendly with the band was an Egyptian musician who played drum. His name was Pierre Fouad... He also invited us to dinner at his home

ctx.x: There was a young couple that came quite often to the Villa d'Este and they eventually became good friends of the band and especially Spider and myself. Their names were Maurice and Venette Cullaz. The father of Venette was Siamese and she was a very beautiful girl with long dark hair. They invited us to dinner in their home; Venette was doing wonderful oriental dishes. I was surprised at the collection of records they had. Maurice had also the records I had made with Fats Waller. They had a little son about two…

Another fellow who became quite friendly with the band was an Egyptian musician who played drum. His name was Pierre Fouad. He had recorded with Django and had quite a solid beat with brushes. He also invited us to dinner at his home and he had a fine collection of records also.

It was there that I heard for the first time Billie Holiday's recording of 'Miss Brown To You' with Teddy Wilson at the box. Fouad also had a photo of Bunny Berigan whom I had heard but never seen. Bunny's recording of 'I Can't Get Started with you' was the greatest he ever did to my estimation. And it is the only record other than some of Louis's that I copied note for note and I still play it the way Bunny did at times just for my own pleasure.
